key_insight: Sequential thermal evaporation follows two different solid-state conversion pathways in perovskite tandem absorbers, so bandgap control must be tailored separately for wide-bandgap and narrow-bandgap stacks.
engineering_relevance: This work provides a solvent-free route to optimize evaporated all-perovskite tandems by controlling precursor composition, conversion kinetics, and vertical composition profiles for higher efficiency and stability.
method: Time-sliced ex situ analysis of sequentially evaporated precursor stacks
Compare conversion behavior in mixed-halide WBG and Sn-Pb NBG absorbers
Use bandgap-targeted sTE recipe optimization based on conversion pathway insights
evidence_signal: The study reports bandgaps from 1.26 to 1.96 eV, a first evaporated all-perovskite tandem solar cell at 19.2% efficiency, and 80% average efficiency retention after 1,200 h at 65 °C.
watch_item: The divergent conversion pathways imply that small changes in precursor thickness, stacking order, or annealing conditions can strongly alter final composition and bandgap uniformity.
paper_title: Divergent Solid-state Conversion Pathways in Evaporated All-perovskite Tandem Solar Cells
